meta.name: Settlement Map
meta.scope: Phase 1. Canada end to end plus the US systems the Canada to US flow touches. Other countries follow in Phase 2.

groups.name: High-value and central bank settlement
groups.definition: Systems where large or time-critical payments settle one by one, or where a central bank holds the accounts everything else settles into.

groups.name: Batch clearing
groups.definition: Systems that collect retail items through the day and settle the net amounts later.

groups.name: Instant payments
groups.definition: Systems where the customer sees the money arrive in seconds. Interbank settlement may be instant or deferred.

groups.name: Card networks
groups.definition: Networks that set card rules and route authorization and clearing between issuers and acquirers.

groups.name: Cross-border messaging and FX settlement
groups.definition: Networks that carry instructions between banks in different countries, or settle both legs of an FX trade together.

groups.name: Stablecoins and tokenized money
groups.definition: Digital tokens redeemable for fiat, with an issuer, a reserve manager and a custodian as separate parties.

groups.name: Customer-facing services
groups.definition: Wallets, apps and super-apps that customers use. They rely on the systems above to move and settle money.

regions.name: United States
regions.note: Only the systems the Canada to US flow touches are loaded in Phase 1.

systems.name: Bank of Canada settlement accounts
systems.participants_summary: Eligible Payments Canada members and, for RTR, payment service providers the Bank supervises under the RPAA. The Bank decides each application.
systems.explainer: The Bank of Canada holds the settlement accounts for Lynx, ACSS and RTR participants. Every Canadian dollar settlement chain on this map ends in these accounts.
caveats: Account access depends on eligibility tests and the Bank's discretion. Holding an account for RTR does not grant one for Lynx.
unknowns: Account hours are not published as a single figure. They follow each system's window.

systems.name: Lynx
systems.hours: Business days. Closed weekends and statutory holidays.
systems.participants_summary: Domestic banks, some foreign bank branches and other financial institutions. Each must hold a settlement account at the Bank of Canada.
systems.explainer: Lynx is Canada's high-value payment system, owned and operated by Payments Canada. Each payment settles on its own, irrevocably and in real time, across participants' Bank of Canada settlement accounts.
caveats: Lynx supports ISO 20022 messages, so remittance data can travel with the payment.
unknowns: Exact daily opening and closing times were not confirmed on the operator page this pass.

systems.name: ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System)
systems.settlement_timing: Previous day's net balances settle the next business morning
systems.hours: Business days. Cheque exchanges run each evening at six regional points.
systems.participants_summary: Direct clearers connect directly and hold Bank of Canada settlement accounts. Indirect clearers clear through a direct clearer.
systems.explainer: ACSS clears cheques and retail electronic items such as direct deposits and pre-authorized debits. Each business morning the previous day's net balances settle, and participants meet those obligations with Lynx payments.
caveats: AFT (direct deposit and pre-authorized debit) items clear through ACSS.
USBE, the US dollar companion, clears USD items in Canada and settles through correspondent banks in New York.
unknowns: Payments Canada does not name Interac products in its ACSS item list.

systems.name: Real-Time Rail (RTR)
systems.participants_summary: Regulated financial institutions and payment service providers the Bank of Canada supervises under the RPAA. Indirect participants settle through an approved direct participant.
systems.explainer: RTR is Payments Canada's planned instant payment system, set for Q4 2026, with exchange, clearing and settlement in real time around the clock. RTR settlement accounts sit on Bank of Canada books and are funded and defunded with Lynx payments.
caveats: Not live as of 2026-10-31. Launch is phased and receiving is required first.
The Bank expects RTR settlement accounts to always hold enough to settle RTR payments.
unknowns: Live participant names are not published yet.

systems.name: Interac e-Transfer
systems.settlement_timing: Day after the value date. Cycles run 00:00 to 23:59 ET.
systems.participants_summary: Direct Connectors connect to the service. Indirect Connectors connect through a Direct Connector or a Connection Service Provider. Downstream Entities reach it through a participant.
systems.explainer: Interac e-Transfer feels instant to customers, but participants settle with each other on a deferred net basis the day after the value date. Interac does not hold participants' funds, and the net obligations settle through Lynx.
caveats: Weekend and holiday transactions can settle up to four days later.
Interac plans to move settlement to RTR, where transactions would clear and settle immediately.
unknowns: Customer-facing hours are not stated in the sources checked.

systems.name: Visa in Canada (VisaNet)
systems.participants_summary: Issuers and acquirers licensed by Visa.
systems.explainer: VisaNet is a card network the Bank of Canada oversees, and Visa sets its rules. Where the CAD net amounts finally settle is not stated in the primary sources checked.
caveats: Card authorization, clearing and settlement happen at different times. Settlement is not instant even when authorization is.
unknowns: CAD settlement path (settlement bank, timing, whether it ends in Lynx) not confirmed from a primary source.

systems.name: Mastercard in Canada (GCMS and SMS)
systems.participants_summary: Issuers and acquirers licensed by Mastercard.
systems.explainer: Mastercard's GCMS and SMS are card systems the Bank of Canada oversees, and Mastercard sets their rules. Where the CAD net amounts finally settle is not stated in the primary sources checked.
caveats: GCMS handles clearing. SMS is Mastercard's single message system.
unknowns: CAD settlement path not confirmed from a primary source.

systems.name: Swift
systems.participants_summary: Banks and other financial institutions that exchange messages on the network.
systems.explainer: Swift is a messaging network that carries payment instructions between banks. It does not hold funds or settle payments.
caveats: A Swift message is an instruction. Money moves only when the banks debit and credit accounts.

systems.name: Federal Reserve master accounts
systems.participants_summary: Eligible depository institutions with a Federal Reserve Bank master account.
systems.explainer: Federal Reserve Banks hold master accounts for eligible institutions. A Fedwire credit to a master account is final.
caveats: Phase 1 loads only what the Canada to US flow touches. FedACH, FedNow, CHIPS and RTP follow in Phase 2.

systems.name: Fedwire Funds Service
systems.settlement_timing: Final when credited to the receiving bank's master account
systems.participants_summary: Institutions with Federal Reserve master accounts.
systems.explainer: Fedwire Funds is the Federal Reserve's high-value funds transfer service. Payments credited to a participant's Federal Reserve master account are final.
caveats: A planned November 2026 Fedwire release was rescheduled to November 2027.
unknowns: Operating hours were not confirmed on the page checked this pass.

scenarios.title: Canada to US business payment by wire
scenarios.summary: A Canadian business pays a US supplier in USD through its bank and a US correspondent.

steps.caption: The payer asks its Canadian bank to send USD to a US account.
The Canadian bank debits the payer's CAD account and converts it to USD. This is a book entry at the bank, not an interbank payment.
The Canadian bank sends a payment instruction to its US correspondent over Swift. Swift carries the message and moves no money.
The correspondent debits the USD account the Canadian bank holds with it.
The correspondent sends the funds over Fedwire. The credit to the payee bank's Federal Reserve master account is final.
The payee's bank credits the payee's USD account.
The payee sees the USD credit.

messaging.text: A Swift instruction between the two banks, then a Fedwire message inside the US.

money.text: Book entries at the Canadian bank (CAD debit) and at the US correspondent (USD account debit).

settlement.text: Only the US leg settles in central bank money, on Federal Reserve books through Fedwire. No CAD interbank settlement happens for this payment.

customer.text: The payer sees one outgoing wire and an FX rate. The payee sees an incoming USD credit.

caveats: If the payee banks with the correspondent itself, step 5 becomes a book transfer and no Fedwire payment happens.
The Canadian bank funds its USD account separately, through its own treasury. Interbank FX can settle in CLS, which is added in Phase 2.
Timing is same day only if both banks act within Fedwire hours.
